text.p: Bayern Munich's campaign to win the German championship was thrown off course when they suffered a calamitous 5-2 defeat at Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday.
The result enabled Borussia Dortmund to finish the weekend on top of the table.

Leverkusen, who were involved in an intense battle to avoid relegation last season, exposed huge holes in the Bavarians' defence, hitting three goals in the first half alone through Brazilian Paulo Sergio, Rene Rydlewicz and Markus Feldhoff.
Bayern made a brief comeback in the second half with goals from Christian Nerlinger and Mario Basler to narrow Leverkusen's lead to 3-2.
But Feldhoff struck again from close range in the 80th minute at a corner and then raced away on his own four minutes later to complete his hat-trick.
The result left reigning champions Dortmund in first place after their 2-1 victory at bottom club Freiburg on Saturday.
Bayern, who started the weekend with a three-point lead over Dortmund, were left level on points and have slipped to second because of an inferior goal difference.
Leverkusen's victory left them third, just two points behind.
